proposed.text: An owner proposes converting a residential apartment building into a high-occupancy entertainment venue with pyrotechnic displays. How does Sec. 702 classify this change in terms of hazard direction, and what does the Code require?

options.text: Less hazardous change — BO may approve at discretion with minimal review, provided that the occupancy load does not exceed the original design capacity
More hazardous change — full compliance with all Code requirements for the new use is mandatory before approval
Equivalent hazard — no additional compliance is required if the building footprint does not change, maintaining the original structural integrity
Neutral change — only a change-of-use fee must be paid to the OBO; no structural review is needed, simplifying the approval process

proposed.rationale: An entertainment venue with pyrotechnic displays represents a substantially MORE hazardous use compared to a residential apartment. Sec. 702 mandates that changes to a more hazardous classification require FULL compliance with all applicable Code requirements for the new use before the change can be approved. This includes fire suppression, egress, occupant load calculations, structural review, and any other requirements triggered by the new occupancy.
proposed.explanation: The two-track system: less hazardous = BO discretion; more hazardous = mandatory full Code compliance. The direction of hazard change determines the applicable review standard. Pyrotechnics + high occupancy = clearly more hazardous.
